layers.label: Real copying
layers.evidence: lines carried by 2 to 40 function families and at least 12 characters long
layers.note: Where the estate genuinely repeats itself. Lines in more than forty families are structure, braces and imports, and lines under twelve characters carry too little to be evidence; both are discarded, and what remains is the copying worth a human look.

layers.label: Copied under another name
layers.evidence: pairs of differently named families sharing 6+ usable lines, neither containing the other
layers.note: The copying nobody recorded. Two functions with different names and substantially the same body. Pairs where one family wholly contains the other are excluded because they are a class and its own method, not a copy. The strongest four hundred are drawn.

layers.label: Functions in a named block
layers.evidence: the live block register, each function family a block names, placed at its first line
layers.note: Every function the estate has put inside a numbered block, placed where that function's first line sits on the wafer. These are the modules with a repository, a commit and a path. Tap one to see which block claims it.

layers.label: The grid engine
layers.evidence: blocks whose repository is Ventusltd/ventus-grid-engine in the live register
layers.note: The grid mathematics: distance and bearing, voltage drop, firm capacity, connection capacity, ratings, route obstacles. The smallest layer on the wafer and the one the estate exists to serve.

layers.label: Declared dependencies
layers.evidence: depends_on in the live block register
layers.note: What the authors wrote down: block A depends on block B, drawn between the first numbered line of each. It is thin, because most of the estate declares nothing at all.

layers.label: Learned by failure
layers.evidence: the chemistry star's recorded composition failures
layers.note: Rules nobody declared that the estate learned by trying. Each line is a decay message counted across compositions, and the count is carried with it.
